I would keep my farm steady and not spread myself too thin. I am 68, I have only 7.5 mu, and I already know the wheat-maize cycle well, so I would still put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because it is the safest part of my farming. I have well irrigation, so I can support the main grain crops and also keep some vegetables for cash income, but I would not push the vegetable area too large because chili and eggplant need more labor, more spraying, and more water. I would divide the land so that my wheat and maize stay on the same main fields, and I would keep smaller plots for cabbage, chili, and eggplant where I can manage them carefully. I would use improved or hybrid seed where it helps stand, yield, and uniformity, and I would fertilize more heavily on vegetables than on grain because vegetables respond more and bring cash. I would irrigate wheat and maize enough to avoid drought loss, and I would use the well more often on vegetables because that is where water gives me a clearer return. I would use rotary tillage for most vegetable ground because it is easier on a small farm, plough for wheat ground before sowing, and I would do maize after wheat with less disturbance to save time. My goal would be stable grain, manageable labor, and some vegetable income without taking on too much risk.
